title: Is Northline ready to launch
scenario: An outdoor brand, Northline, plans to launch an AI-made ad set on Friday. You run the go or no-go meeting. Use the exhibit. The brand, the gate sheet, the test and the clip times are made up for this case. The vendor lines are copied from the docs. The gate is our own tool, not a vendor rule.
exhibit:
GATE SHEET (ours, filled in for this case):
  Provenance  master folder kept, export path tested     YES
  Signals     press line makes no promise about traceability   YES
  Labels      YouTube label decided; TikTok label not decided  NO
  Limits      sum checked, ramp planned, staging test done     YES
  Incidents   one-page plan filled in, with names              YES
  Review      a person has looked at each asset                YES

TEST (made up for this case):
  50 prompts through the brand tool. 48 pass, 2 fail: 96 out of 100 on average.
  Both failures made a look-alike of a real person.

AD SET (made up for this case): 30 still images and 4 Veo 3.1 clips.

CLIPS (made up for this case), now is Thursday 12:00. None is downloaded yet.
  V1  Veo 3.1 clip generated Monday 09:00
  V2  Veo 3.1 clip generated Wednesday 15:00
  V3  Veo 3.1 clip generated Thursday 08:00
  V4  an extension of V2, generated Wednesday 17:00

VENDOR LINES (copied from the docs):
  OpenAI: "Wherever possible, we recommend having a human review outputs before they are used in practice." Humans should "have access to any information needed to verify the outputs".
  Google: "you may want to focus on worst-case performance across your evaluation set rather than average performance."
  Google, Veo 3.1: "Generated videos are stored on the server for 2 days, after which they are removed." "Extended videos are treated as newly generated videos."
  YouTube: creators answer the "AI use" question during upload in YouTube Studio.

questions.prompt: The Review line says YES. For that YES to count, who should have reviewed the 30 ad images, and with what?

options.text: A named person who is given the brief, the master files and the rules
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says humans should have access to the information needed to verify the outputs. For media that is the brief, the masters and the rules.

options.text: The tool's own quality score, because a machine is faster than any person
options.explanation: OpenAI recommends human review where possible. A score from the same tool is not a person's check.

options.text: A person who sees only a slideshow of the final images, to keep it quick
options.explanation: A reviewer who sees only the final images cannot check them against the brief or the masters.

options.text: Any person on the team, as long as the brief stays with the project manager
options.explanation: Without the brief and the masters, the reviewer cannot check the work.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with calling the test a pass at 96 out of 100?

options.text: Every test must score 100 out of 100, and nothing below counts as a pass
options.explanation: No source asks for a perfect score. Google says to set the minimum levels before testing.

options.text: Fifty prompts is too small a test, so it can never show anything useful
options.explanation: The size is not the main problem. Even a small test can show a clear weak spot.

options.text: The average hides the worst case, as both failures made real-person look-alikes
options.explanation: Right. Google suggests judging worst-case performance. The failures are all in one serious category, so the rule must be fixed.

options.text: Nothing, because a reviewer will catch every failure after the launch day
options.explanation: Human review helps, but it is not a reason to ignore a known failure in testing.

questions.prompt: Using the Veo line, which clips can still be downloaded at Thursday 12:00?

options.text: V1, V2 and V3, because the extension V4 is just part of V2
options.explanation: V1 is 3 days old, so its server copy is gone. V4 is treated as newly generated.

options.text: V2, V3 and V4, because V1 is older than 2 days and V4 is new
options.explanation: Right. V1 is older than 2 days. V4 counts as new, from Wednesday 17:00, so it is still there.

options.text: All four, because the server keeps every video until it is deleted
options.explanation: Google says generated videos are removed after 2 days.

options.text: V3 only, because every clip made before today is already gone
options.explanation: The limit is 2 days, not the calendar date. V2 and V4 are younger than 2 days.

options.text: Release to everyone at once, so that every customer sees the same thing on day one
options.explanation: A full release leaves no room to stop early if something is wrong.

options.text: Start with a small internal group, and decide the pass level and the stop signs first
options.explanation: Right. Set the bar before the test, widen only when the earlier step passes, and know in advance what makes you stop.

options.text: Start with a small group, and decide what counts as a failure after seeing the results
options.explanation: Google says to think about the minimum acceptable levels before testing. Setting the bar afterwards bends the result.

options.text: Skip the small group, because the 50-prompt test already covered every case
options.explanation: A test with 50 prompts cannot cover real users, and it showed a weak spot.

questions.prompt: What is the right result of the meeting, given the gate sheet?

options.text: Go, because five of the six lines on the gate sheet are marked YES
options.explanation: The gate needs every blocking line to be YES. Labels is a NO.

options.text: Go now, and decide the TikTok label after the post is already live
options.explanation: If the post goes live first, it goes live without a decided label. The gate exists so labels are decided before anyone uploads.

options.text: Cancel the whole campaign, since one line of the gate sheet shows a NO
options.explanation: A NO means fix that line, not give up the campaign.

options.text: No-go until the TikTok label is decided, then launch when it is YES
options.explanation: Right. One blocking NO means no launch yet. Decide the TikTok label, mark the line YES, then launch.
